topic: Why a refund shrinks or turns into a balance owing with the same salary: refund = tax withheld − tax payable; RRSP deduction, single job, two jobs each claiming the basic personal amount (2026, Manitoba example)

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Manitoba resident, employment income only, 2026 tables (CRA T4127 Jan/Jul 2026 via longform/tools/taxcalc.py: federal 14% to $58,523, 20.5% to $117,045; Manitoba 10.8% to $47,000, 12.75% to $100,000; BPA $16,452 / $15,780; CPP/EI credits). Year 1: payroll withholding assumed equal to the tax on $70,000; the $6,000 RRSP deduction falls entirely in the 20.5% + 12.75% bands (taxable $69,335 → $63,335). Year 3: under-withholding estimated as tax on $70,000 minus twice the tax on $35,000 (each payroll treating its job as the only one, full credits on both TD1s); real payroll formulas differ slightly.

sources.refund: CRA T1 return: line 43700 = total income tax deducted from all slips (T4 box 22); line 48400 refund = line 48200 total credits − line 43500 total payable; otherwise 48500 balance owing (CRA general guide / CVITP material, via search results 2026-10-13)
sources.td1: CRA 'Get the completed TD1 forms' (canada.ca) and Form TD1 2026: with more than one employer or payer at the same time, personal credits already claimed can't be claimed again; if total income will exceed them, tick the box, enter 0 on line 13; BPA $16,452 (2026); the form also lets you ask for additional tax to be deducted
sources.rates: 2026 federal brackets 14% / 20.5% (from $58,523) (CRA indexation, news reports Dec 2025; T4127 2026) and Manitoba 2026 (frozen brackets, verified for H4): via longform/tools/taxcalc.py
